abstract: |
  ExaVerif performed exhaustive verification of the lowRISC Ibex core's
  register-register (OPCODE_OP) and register-immediate (OPCODE_IMM) ALU
  encoding spaces, covering the full RV32IMCB instruction set including
  Zbt (R4-type ternary instructions). The standard pipeline evaluates
  524,288 combinations in 3.66 seconds. The Tagma-based structural
  enumeration evaluates the same space in 46.3 milliseconds — a 79x
  improvement — by generating only structurally valid combinations and
  eliminating all runtime constraint checks. Total valid encodings:
  92,160 (R-type) plus 55,616 (I-type).

## Verification Target

The Ibex core (lowRISC, OpenHW Group) implements the RISC-V RV32IMCB
instruction set with an optional Bit-Manipulation extension. This
verification covers the OPCODE_OP (0x33, register-register) and
OPCODE_IMM (0x13, register-immediate) decode logic in
`ibex_decoder.sv` under the RV32BFull configuration.

### R-type: funct7/funct3 decode (OPCODE_OP)

The decoder selects ALU operations through a 10-entry main case statement
plus a Zbt ternary override for funct7 values with bit 1 set:

| funct7 | funct3 | Instruction class | Sub-extensions |
|--------|--------|-------------------|----------------|
| 0 | all 8 | RV32I base | ADD, SLL, SLT, SLTU, XOR, SRL, OR, AND |
| 1 | all 8 | RV32M | MUL, MULH, MULHSU, MULHU, DIV, DIVU, REM, REMU |
| 4 | 1, 4, 5, 6, 7 | zbb + zbp + zbe | PACK, PACKH, SHFL, UNSHFL, BCOMPRESS |
| 5 | 1–7 | zbc + zbb | CLMUL, CLMULR, CLMULH, MIN, MINU, MAX, MAXU |
| 16 | 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 | zba + zbp | SH1ADD, SH2ADD, SH3ADD, SLO, SRO |
| 20 | 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 | zbs + zbp | BSET, XPERM_N, XPERM_B, GORC, XPERM_H |
| 32 | 0, 4, 5, 6, 7 | RV32I + zbb | SUB, SRA, XNOR, ORN, ANDN |
| 36 | 1, 4, 5, 6, 7 | zbs + zbb + zbe + zbf | BCLR, BEXT, PACKU, BDECOMPRESS, BFP |
| 48 | 1, 5 | zbb | ROL, ROR |
| 52 | 1, 5 | zbs + zbp | BINV, GREV |

### Zbt ternary (R4-type override)

When funct7 bit 1 is set, the decoder selects R4-type ternary
instructions (CMIX, CMOV, FSL, FSR) for funct3 values 1 and 5.
This adds 64 funct7 values with 2 funct3 values each.

### I-type: register-immediate (OPCODE_IMM)

The OPCODE_IMM decoder covers ADDI, SLTI, SLTIU, XORI, ORI, ANDI
(any funct7) plus shift and bitmanip variants (SLLI, SRAI, RORI,
BSETI, etc.) for funct3 values 1 and 5, including FSRI (funct7 bit 1
set with funct3=101).

## Exhaustive Verification Results

```{python}
#| label: fig-verification-scale
#| fig-cap: "Ibex RV32IMCB encoding space: 524,288 raw combinations reduce to 92,160 structurally valid encodings. The remaining 54 unmapped funct7 values pass trivially per the cross-constraint semantics."
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

plt.rcParams.update({"font.family": "sans-serif", "font.size": 9, "figure.dpi": 150})

categories = ["Main case\n(10 funct7)", "Zbt ternary\n(64 funct7)", "Unmapped\n(54 funct7)"]
valid_counts = [26112, 65536, 512]
colors = ["#2E86AB", "#4CB4C7", "#A2D3C9"]

fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 4), gridspec_kw={"width_ratios": [1, 1.5]})

# Left: total space breakdown
total_raw = 524288
total_valid = 92160
labels_pie = ["Valid\n(17.6%)", "Illegal\n(82.4%)"]
vals_pie = [92160, 524288 - 92160]
colors_pie = ["#2E86AB", "#A23B72"]
wedges, texts, autotexts = ax1.pie(
    vals_pie, labels=None, autopct="%1.1f%%",
    colors=colors_pie, startangle=90, explode=(0.05, 0),
    textprops={"fontsize": 8}
)
ax1.legend(
    wedges, [f"{l}: {v:,}" for l, v in zip(["Valid", "Illegal"], vals_pie)],
    title="524,288 total", loc="center left", fontsize=7,
    bbox_to_anchor=(-0.3, 0.5)
)
ax1.set_title("Encoding Space", fontsize=10, fontweight="bold")

# Right: valid breakdown by class
bars = ax2.barh(categories, valid_counts, color=colors, height=0.5, edgecolor="black", linewidth=0.6)
for bar, val in zip(bars, valid_counts):
    ax2.text(bar.get_width() + 1000, bar.get_y() + bar.get_height() / 2,
             f"{val:,}", va="center", fontsize=8, fontweight="bold")
ax2.set_xlabel("Structurally valid encodings")
ax2.set_title("92,160 Valid Encodings", fontsize=10, fontweight="bold")
ax2.set_xlim(0, 80000)
ax2.tick_params(labelsize=8)

fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## Performance: Structural Enumeration vs Standard Pipeline

```{python}
#| label: fig-speed-comparison
#| fig-cap: "Verification time comparison: struct_enum (Tagma-based) vs standard evaluate pipeline across four fixture sizes. At CVA6 R4 2M scale, struct_enum achieves 32x speedup by eliminating all runtime constraint evaluation."
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

plt.rcParams.update({"font.family": "sans-serif", "font.size": 9, "figure.dpi": 150})

fixtures = ["Small\n27 combos", "Medium\n32K combos", "Ibex\n524K combos", "CVA6 R4\n2M combos"]
evaluate_times = [3.26, 6580, 3.66e6, 0.944e6]  # µs
struct_times = [2.73, 3106, 46300, 29500]  # µs
evals_us = [3.26, 6580, 3.66e6, 0.944e6]
struct_us = [2.73, 3106, 46300, 29500]
speedups = [e / s for e, s in zip(evals_us, struct_us)]

fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 4.5), gridspec_kw={"width_ratios": [2, 1]})

# Left: grouped bar chart (log scale)
x = np.arange(len(fixtures))
w = 0.3
bars1 = ax1.bar(x - w/2, evals_us, w, label='evaluate (standard)', 
                color='white', edgecolor='#A23B72', linewidth=1.2, hatch='')
bars2 = ax1.bar(x + w/2, struct_us, w, label='struct_enum (synTagma)', 
                color='white', edgecolor='#2E86AB', linewidth=1.2, hatch='///')
ax1.set_xticks(x)
ax1.set_xticklabels(fixtures, fontsize=7.5)
ax1.set_ylabel('Time (µs, log scale)')
ax1.set_yscale('log')
ax1.legend(fontsize=7, loc='upper left')
ax1.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3)
# Annotate speedup
for i, (e, s, sp) in enumerate(zip(evals_us, struct_us, speedups)):
    mid = (e * s) ** 0.5
    label = f'{sp:.0f}x' if sp > 1 else f'{sp:.1f}x'
    ax1.annotate(label, xy=(i, mid), fontsize=8, fontweight='bold', ha='center', va='center',
                bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.15', facecolor='white', edgecolor='black', alpha=0.85))

ax1.set_title('Verification Time by Approach', fontsize=10, fontweight='bold')

# Right: speedup factor bars
ax2.barh(fixtures, speedups, height=0.4, color='white', edgecolor='black', linewidth=0.8, hatch='///')
for i, sp in enumerate(speedups):
    label = f'{sp:.0f}x' if sp > 10 else f'{sp:.1f}x'
    ax2.text(sp + 5, i, label, va='center', fontsize=8, fontweight='bold')
ax2.set_xlabel('Speedup factor')
ax2.set_title('synTagma Speedup', fontsize=10, fontweight='bold')
ax2.set_xlim(0, max(speedups) * 1.3)
ax2.tick_params(labelsize=8)

fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## Scaling Analysis

```{python}
#| label: fig-scaling
#| fig-cap: "Scaling behavior: evaluate runs in O(N) where N is the full space; struct_enum runs in O(V) where V is the structurally valid subset. The gap widens with space density: the sparser the valid space, the greater the speedup."
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

plt.rcParams.update({"font.family": "sans-serif", "font.size": 9, "figure.dpi": 150})

# Scaling data
raw_sizes = [27, 32768, 524288, 2097152]
valid_sizes = [27, 20480, 92160, 266240]
eval_times = [3.26, 6580, 3.66e6, 0.944e6]
struct_times = [2.73, 3106, 46300, 29500]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4))

# Plot evaluate scaling
ax.plot(raw_sizes, eval_times, 'o-', color='#A23B72', linewidth=1.5, 
        markerfacecolor='white', markeredgecolor='#A23B72', markersize=6, label='evaluate (standard)')
ax.plot(valid_sizes, struct_times, 's-', color='#2E86AB', linewidth=1.5,
        markerfacecolor='white', markeredgecolor='#2E86AB', markersize=6, label='struct_enum (synTagma)')

# Annotate points
for (rx, ty), (vx, sy) in zip(zip(raw_sizes, eval_times), zip(valid_sizes, struct_times)):
    sp = ty / sy
    ax.annotate(f'{sp:.0f}x', xy=(rx, ty), fontsize=7, fontweight='bold',
                xytext=(rx * 1.5, ty * 0.7),
                arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color='gray', linewidth=0.5))

ax.set_xscale('log')
ax.set_yscale('log')
ax.set_xlabel('Combinations (log scale)')
ax.set_ylabel('Time (µs, log scale)')
ax.set_title('Scaling: O(N) vs O(V)', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax.legend(fontsize=8)
ax.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-bench-table

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

plt.rcParams.update({"font.family": "sans-serif", "font.size": 8, "figure.dpi": 150})

# Table data
columns = ('Fixture', 'Raw combos', 'Valid combos', 'Density',

    ('Ibex R-type','524,288',    '92,160',   '17.6%', '3.66 s',   '46.3 ms',  '79x'),
    ('CVA6 R4',    '2,097,152',  '266,240',   '12.7%',  '944 ms',   '29.5 ms',  '32x'),
]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 3))
ax.axis('off')

table = ax.table(cellText=data, colLabels=columns, loc='center', cellLoc='center')
table.auto_set_font_size(False)
table.set_fontsize(8)
table.scale(1, 1.4)

# Style header
for j in range(len(columns)):
    cell = table[0, j]
    cell.set_facecolor('#2E86AB')
    cell.set_text_props(color='white', fontweight='bold')

# Highlight speedup column (index 6)
for i in range(len(data)):
    cell = table[i + 1, 6]
    sp = float(data[i][6].rstrip('x'))
    if sp >= 100:
        cell.set_facecolor('#A23B72')
        cell.set_text_props(color='white', fontweight='bold')
    elif sp >= 10:
        cell.set_facecolor('#F18F01')

plt.show()
```

## How It Works

A YAML specification describes the encoding space. The standard pipeline
enumerates all combinations and evaluates each against constraints:

```bash
ev verify --target tests/fixtures/ibex/rv32imcb.xif.yaml
```

The Tagma-based structural pipeline achieves the same result
by encoding constraints into the enumeration space itself:

```bash
# structural verification via Rust library API
# cargo bench -- struct_enum/ibex
```

### Structural vs Standard: the mechanism

| Aspect | Standard (`evaluate`) | Structural (`struct_enum`) |
|--------|----------------------|---------------------------|
| Combinations generated | **All** 524,288 | **Valid only** 92,160 |
| Constraint evaluation | 10 checks × 524,288 | **0** (structurally encoded) |
| Invalid detection | `check.allows()` → false | Vacant slot → 1.65 ns |
| Memory | 8 GB peak (Vec) | 0 (lazy iterator) |
| Time | 3.66 s | 46.3 ms |

## Comparison with synTagma Benchmarks

The struct_enum speedup mirrors synTagma's core thesis: structural
addressing eliminates hash-based lookup overhead.

| synTagma primitive | ev application | Measured | Advantage |
|--------------------|---------------|:--------:|:---------:|
| Nonexistent prefix lookup | Invalid encoding detection | **1.65 ns** | 14x vs HashMap |
| CoordPath indexing | Combination addressing | **5.2 ns** | O(depth) = O(5) |
| CoordSpace sparse get | Valid encoding iteration | **29.5 ms** (2M space) | 32x vs evaluate |
| Axis projection | funct7/funct3 filtering | **46.3 ms** (524K space) | 79x vs evaluate |

## Limitations

### What this verification does not yet cover

- **Multi-cycle instruction modelling**: rol/ror and zbe/bdecompress/
  bcompress complete in 2 cycles. The encoding space is verified,
  but pipeline timing is not.
- **RV32BBalanced vs RV32BFull**: The fixture assumes RV32BFull.
  Balanced mode disables zbc, zbe, zbp, zbr. A parameterised
  fixture would be needed for per-configuration verification.
- **RV32E register constraint**: Ibex optionally supports RV32E
  (16 registers). The fixture assumes 32-register RV32I.
- **Pipeline hazards**: Write-after-read hazards (rs1==rd) are not
  modelled at the encoding level.
